---
title: "Example: mapping access to jobs and schools"
description: >
  Travel times from one point to a grid, and the jobs and schools reachable
  within 30 minutes from every cell of Porto Alegre, walking and by public
  transport.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.9, dpi = 110, out.width = "100%")
```

How many jobs can people reach from where they live? This example answers
that for Porto Alegre, on a grid of hexagonal cells, first walking and then
walking with public transport, and draws the answer as a map. Everything
below is one script; the output shown is the output it prints.

## The data

The Porto Alegre sample of r5r 2.5.0 (an OpenStreetMap extract, the bus and
train GTFS feeds, and a grid of 1,227 hexagonal cells with their population,
jobs and schools), downloaded once into a temporary directory:

```{r download, message = FALSE}
library(peabiru)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

poa <- file.path(tempdir(), "poa")
dir.create(poa, showWarnings = FALSE)
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipea/r5r/v2.5.0/r-package/inst/extdata/poa/"
for (f in c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_eptc.zip", "poa_trensurb.zip",
            "poa_hexgrid.csv", "poa_points_of_interest.csv")) {
  if (!file.exists(file.path(poa, f))) {
    download.file(paste0(url, f), file.path(poa, f), mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  }
}

network <- build_network(poa)
grid <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_hexgrid.csv"))
head(grid)
colSums(grid[, c("population", "schools", "jobs")], na.rm = TRUE)
```

Each cell is a point at its centre. The bus feed of the sample only has trips
between late morning and early evening on weekdays, so public transport is
routed from 14:00 on a Monday, over a 30-minute window of departures.

```{r departure}
departure <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")
```

## Travel times from one point

A first look: the travel time from one place, Farroupilha Park, to the centre
of every cell. `travel_time_matrix()` leaves out the pairs that take longer
than `max_trip_duration`.

```{r ttm}
poi <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_points_of_interest.csv"))
park <- poi[poi$id == "farroupilha_park", ]

from_park <- rbind(
  data.frame(mode = "Walking", travel_time_matrix(
    network, park, grid, mode = "WALK", max_trip_duration = 60)),
  data.frame(mode = "Walking + public transport", travel_time_matrix(
    network, park, grid, mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
    departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 30, max_trip_duration = 60))
)
sapply(split(from_park$travel_time_p50, from_park$mode),
       function(t) c(cells = length(t), median_minutes = median(t)))
```

Within an hour, public transport reaches about four times as many cells as
walking does. On a map, with each cell drawn as a dot at its centre:

```{r ttm-map, fig.alt = "Two maps of Porto Alegre made of dots, one per grid cell reached within an hour of Farroupilha Park, coloured by travel time: walking reaches a compact patch around the park; with public transport, dots cover most of the city, the closest ones along the bus corridors."}
cells <- st_as_sf(grid, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
map <- merge(cells, from_park, by.x = "id", by.y = "to_id")
ggplot(map) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = travel_time_p50), size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#7a3318", high = "#f5d3b6", name = "Minutes") +
  facet_wrap(~mode) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```

## Jobs and schools within 30 minutes

`accessibility()` adds up, for each origin, the opportunities at every
destination reached within the cutoff (the `"step"` decay function, the
default). Five cells have no job count; they count as zero, with a warning.

```{r access}
access <- rbind(
  data.frame(mode = "Walking", accessibility(
    network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),
    mode = "WALK", cutoffs = 30)),
  data.frame(mode = "Walking + public transport", accessibility(
    network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),
    mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), departure_datetime = departure,
    time_window = 30, cutoffs = 30))
)
head(access)
```

Weighting each cell by the people who live there gives what the average
resident reaches:

```{r average}
access <- merge(access, grid[, c("id", "population")], by = "id")
sapply(split(access, list(access$opportunity, access$mode)), function(a)
  round(weighted.mean(a$accessibility, a$population)))
```

Public transport roughly triples both: about 21 thousand jobs and 12
schools within half an hour on foot, against 68 thousand jobs and 31
schools with the buses and the train.

And the map of jobs reachable from each cell:

```{r access-map, fig.alt = "Two maps of Porto Alegre made of dots, one per grid cell, coloured by the number of jobs reachable within 30 minutes: walking, only the city centre reaches more than 50 thousand; with public transport, the centre and the corridors leading to it reach more than 100 thousand."}
jobs <- merge(cells, access[access$opportunity == "jobs", ], by = "id")
ggplot(jobs) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = accessibility / 1000), size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#e3eadb", high = "#1f5139",
                        name = "Thousand jobs") +
  facet_wrap(~mode) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```

## Variations

- **Gradual access.** `decay_function = "logistic"` (or `"exponential"`,
  `"linear"`, `"fixed_exponential"`) weights every job by its travel time
  instead of counting those under a hard limit; see the article
  [Accessibility](accessibility.html).
- **Several cutoffs at once.** `cutoffs = c(15, 30, 45)` returns one row per
  cutoff, from a single routing pass.
- **Percentiles.** With `percentiles = c(25, 50, 75)`, the accessibility of
  a good, a typical and a bad departure in the window.

The maps on the [home page](../../index.html#gallery) draw the same results
as hexagons, with `site/figures/figures.R` in the repository.
